claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^–4–10^–2 s^–1.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance at high temperature.
Exposing the alloy to an Al-rich powder pack at approximately 1100 °C for 5–10 hours under an inert or mildly reducing atmosphere will cause aluminum to diffuse into its surface.
Pack aluminization can confine aluminum diffusion mainly to the surface without significantly changing the bulk composition.
Pack aluminization will produce a uniform, thin, adherent Al2O3 surface layer on equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Aluminum delivered by pack aluminization will react with ambient or residual oxygen to form a continuous Al2O3 scale.
The Al2O3 scale will act as a diffusion barrier that retards oxygen ingress.
Retarding oxygen ingress will enhance the oxidation resistance of the alloy at approximately 1000 °C.
Limiting aluminization to the surface will leave the bulk microstructure minimally affected.
Preserving the bulk microstructure will preserve the alloy's room-temperature ductility and high-temperature yield strength.
Relative to untreated specimens, aluminized specimens will show slower oxide-scale growth at 1000 °C.
Relative to untreated specimens, aluminized specimens will show lower oxygen uptake at 1000 °C.
After aluminization and oxidation exposure, room-temperature tensile ductility will remain within 8–16%.
After aluminization and oxidation exposure, yield strength at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^–4–10^–2 s^–1 will remain within 163–530 MPa.
Excessive aluminum penetration could alter phase equilibria or reduce ductility.
Inappropriate aluminization conditions could form deleterious intermetallic phases in the alloy interior.
The protective scale may have uncertain stability during cyclic or prolonged high-temperature exposure.
